prompt: Beatriz studies Topic A on Monday from 8 to 9 p.m. using practice questions, then sleeps normally that night. She studies Topic B on Tuesday from 8 to 9 p.m. in exactly the same way, but that night she is up until 4 a.m. on a family airport trip — not studying — and then sleeps normally from Wednesday to Sunday. A test the following Monday covers both topics, and she recalls Topic A much better than Topic B, even though B was studied a day later. What best explains the difference?

options.text: Topic A had one extra day to be forgotten, so its advantage must mean Topic B was simply the harder material
Studying later in the week always produces weaker memory, regardless of what happens afterwards

Sleep in the period soon after learning supports consolidation of that material; losing most of the night right after studying B weakened its retention, and her later normal nights did not fully make up for that specific loss
She recalled A better because Monday studying is always more effective than Tuesday studying at the same time of day

explanation: The deciding detail is when the lost sleep fell: on the night immediately after Topic B was studied, while Topic A was followed by a normal night. Sleep after learning is linked to memory consolidation, and the several normal nights before the test rule out her simply being tired on test day as the main explanation.
